items.original_text: Filing step: File a Place of Entertainment permit application with the SF Entertainment Commission in parallel with the CUA, after an intake meeting to confirm POE classification. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm eligibility and schedule an intake meeting. State that the CUA application is filed with Planning and that the bar will comply with the Good Neighbor Policy. The Commission will confirm whether the concept qualifies as POE (likely yes, given amplified sound and late hours) or LLP (unlikely). File the POE application with the $2,708 fee (2026–27), post the required 30-day yellow notice at the premises, and coordinate the hearing date with the CUA hearing at Planning so both approvals are decided in the same cycle.

items.original_text: Filing step: File a Health Permit to Operate application with SF DPH after the building permit is issued and the DPH plan check is approved, and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Submit the online Health Permit application with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN at least one month before the target opening date. Upload the approved DPH plan check, proof of a certified food safety manager on staff (ServSafe or equivalent certificate), and the menu (limited food: small plates, panini, reheating). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection when construction is 80% complete; the inspector will verify that the kitchen layout, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and ventilation match the approved plans. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes, and service to the public cannot begin before issuance.

ABC will send the application to SFPD (ABC Liaison Unit) and SF Planning for referral review; Planning will issue a letter confirming the CUA authorizes a Bar with Type 42 license under Mission SUD § 249.60(b)(2)(C). Post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days and mail copies to all residents and businesses within 500 ft. If no protests are filed, ABC will approve the transfer in 60 to 90 days. If a protest is filed alleging undue concentration or public convenience issues, budget an additional 60 to 120 days for a public hearing and a PCN finding from the Board of Supervisors.

items.original_text: Filing step: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, California seller's permit, EIN, RBS training for all alcohol servers, food handler cards, and ASCAP/BMI music licenses before opening. What to say: File the SF Business Registration online with the Treasurer & Tax Collector ($55 to $700 depending on projected gross receipts, plus $4 state fee) immediately after forming the legal entity. Obtain the EIN from the IRS (free, same-day online), then register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA (free, needed for the ABC application). Enroll all employees who will serve alcohol in the ABC RBS training ($3 registration plus $10 to $25 course fee per person) within 60 days of hire. Enroll all food-handling employees in the California Food Handler Card course ($7 to $15, valid 3 years). Designate at least one certified food safety manager (ServSafe exam, $100 to $250). Sign up for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses (annual fees roughly $300 to $2,500 each, formula-based on occupancy and music use) to cover recorded and live music legally.

items.original_text: Estimated time: 185 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $7,941 to $23,750. Notes: The timeline and cost ranges cover the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45 to 120 days, $2,708 to $3,800), Health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000), and Building permit with change of use (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000). The day range is the time to approval, not to a denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (6 to 10 months from filing to final, including pre-application meeting, environmental review, neighborhood notification, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period) followed by the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60 to 150 days after the CUA is final, including escrow, posting, referrals, and undue-concentration review if protested). The POE permit hearing is scheduled in parallel with the CUA and decided within the same cycle. The building permit and health permit are filed after the CUA is approved and run concurrently during construction (3 to 6 months for plan review, build-out, and inspections). Total elapsed time from CUA filing to opening: roughly 12 to 18 months if the CUA and ABC transfer are approved without appeals or protests. Costs include the CUA fee ($3,100 base, higher if construction valuation exceeds thresholds or First Year Free fee waiver does not apply), POE application fee ($2,708 in 2026–27), building permit fees (percentage of construction cost, estimated $800 to $15,000 for a bar tenant improvement), DPH plan check ($828 to $2,207 depending on scope), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), and the ABC Type 42 license purchase price (not a government fee, estimated $20,000 to $60,000 based on market comparables for Type 42 transfers in San Francisco, excluded from the cost range here). Additional costs not in the range: architect and engineer fees for stamped plans, license broker commission (typically 10% to 15% of the license price), construction costs, and pre-opening legal and consultant fees. The cost range shown is government fees only.

items.original_text: Filing step: File a Health Permit to Operate application with SF DPH after the building permit is issued and the DPH plan check is approved, and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Submit the online Health Permit application with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN at least one month before the target opening date. Upload the approved DPH plan check, proof of a certified food safety manager on staff (ServSafe or equivalent certificate), and the menu (limited food: small plates, panini, reheating). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection when construction is 80% complete; the inspector will verify that the kitchen layout, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and ventilation match the approved plans. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes, and service to the public cannot begin before issuance.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Operating hours limited to 6 a.m. to 2 a.m., consistent with NCT-VALENCIA principally permitted hours; hours between 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. are a conditional use. Basis: NCT-VALENCIA § 762 sets principally permitted hours at 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. and conditional hours at 2 a.m. to 6 a.m. The concept's 1 a.m. closing falls within the principally permitted window, but the CUA may condition the exact closing hour and prohibit extension without Commission approval.
outcomes.note: The record does not state operating hours or time restrictions for NCT-VALENCIA.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Good Neighbor Policy conditions under Police Code § 1060 and Planning Code § 202.2, including security plan, sound limits, litter and graffiti abatement, and liaison with neighborhood groups. Basis: Mission SUD § 249.60(d) requires all liquor establishments to comply with § 202.2 operating conditions. A 2026 Project Profile at 2500 Mission states 'Use is subject to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy' for nighttime entertainment. Comparable POE permits and CUAs for bars and entertainment venues in the Mission corridor carried similar conditions.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Exterior lighting, window signage limited to 33% of window area, and 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades, per Mission SUD § 249.60(d). Basis: Mission SUD § 249.60(d) imposes these physical design requirements on all new, relocated, or expanded liquor establishments in the district. The CUA will condition compliance with these standards and may require design review by Planning before the building permit is issued.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Type 42 beer-and-wine license only; no upgrade to Type 47 or Type 48 full-liquor license without a new CUA and Planning Commission hearing. Basis: The CUA will authorize a Bar use with a specific ABC license type (Type 42). A 2011 CUA at 991–999 Valencia approved upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47, showing that license-type changes require separate Commission approval. A condition will prohibit changing the license type or mode of operation without amending the CUA.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: No expansion of square footage devoted to bar use or substantial change in mode of operation without Planning review, consistent with Mission SUD § 249.60 restrictions on existing alcohol establishments. Basis: A 2006 agency referral at 1101 Valencia approved license continuation with a condition: 'Not to expand the original square footage of the existing bar on the premises,' citing Mission SUD restrictions. New bars will face parallel conditions to prevent intensification of alcohol sales in the district.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Entertainment area and amplified sound limits set by the Entertainment Commission's POE permit conditions, potentially including sound studies, soundproofing, and ending live shows by 11 p.m. or midnight. Basis: The 2014 POE referral at 998 Valencia limited entertainment to one-third of gross floor area under Police Code § 1060(r). Recent POE permits in the Mission corridor carry sound limits and Good Neighbor conditions. Although the concept closes at 1 a.m., the Commission may condition earlier end times for amplified entertainment to mitigate residential impacts.

outcomes.original: Expected condition: Validity period of three years from the effective date of the CUA motion; the Type 42 license transfer must be completed within that period or the authorization expires. Basis: The 2023 CUA at 999 Valencia for a Type 20 license conditioned: 'The authorization is valid for three years; the ABC shall have initiated the license transfer in conformity with State law timeframes or this period lapses.' Standard CUA validity language requires diligent pursuit of the approved use within three years.
outcomes.note: The 2023 CUA was for a Type 20 license (not Type 42) and required the transfer be 'initiated' (not completed) within three years.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for a Bar use at 995 Valencia St, including a project description, floor plans showing the bar area and entertainment space, a Good Neighbor plan, and the Mission SUD license-source documentation. What to say: The application narrative should state: 'This is a change of use from Restaurant (existing Type 41 at 995 Valencia, Sarita's Grill & Beer) to Bar under Planning Code § 102, requiring CUA under NCT-VALENCIA § 762 and Mission SUD § 249.60(b)(2)(C). The bar will hold a Type 42 on-sale beer-and-wine license transferred from [address of source bar within the Mission SUD]. The 40-seat bar will serve limited food (small plates, panini, reheating), feature live entertainment with amplified sound, and close at 1 a.m. nightly. Hours fall within the principally permitted window (6 a.m. to 2 a.m.). The operator will comply with Mission SUD § 249.60(d) design requirements (exterior lighting, 33% window signage limit, 50% clear glazing) and Planning Code § 202.2 Good Neighbor operating conditions.' Attach a security and sound plan, a neighborhood outreach summary, and the Entertainment Commission POE…

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Place of Entertainment permit application with the SF Entertainment Commission in parallel with the CUA, after an intake meeting to confirm POE classification. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm eligibility and schedule an intake meeting. At intake, describe the concept: live entertainment (solo and small bands) with amplified sound, closing at 1 a.m., in a 40-seat bar with limited food service. State that the CUA application is filed with Planning and that the bar will comply with the Good Neighbor Policy. The Commission will confirm whether the concept qualifies as POE (likely yes, given amplified sound and late hours) or LLP (unlikely). File the POE application with the $2,708 fee (2026–27), post the required 30-day yellow notice at the premises, and coordinate the hearing date with the CUA hearing at Planning so both approvals are decided in the same cycle.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a building permit application with SF DBI for tenant improvements and change of use from Restaurant to Bar, routed to Planning, DPH, Fire, and PUC for FOG review. What to say: The building permit application should reference the CUA case number and state: 'Change of use from Restaurant to Bar per CUA [case number]; tenant improvements include new bar fixture, kitchen hood (limited cooking), interior finishes, ADA restroom upgrades, and electrical/plumbing for entertainment sound system. No change of occupancy is anticipated (existing and proposed occupancy both Group B, occupant load < 50), but DBI will confirm from the floor plan.' Submit two sets of stamped architectural plans, a DPH plan check application for the limited kitchen ($828 to $2,207 fee), and a FOG Installation Verification Form if installing or modifying a grease interceptor. The building permit will not be issued until the CUA is approved and the motion is final (after the 30-day appeal period).

outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Health Permit to Operate application with SF DPH after the building permit is issued and the DPH plan check is approved, and schedule the pre-opening inspection. What to say: Submit the online Health Permit application with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN at least one month before the target opening date. Upload the approved DPH plan check, proof of a certified food safety manager on staff (ServSafe or equivalent certificate), and the menu (limited food: small plates, panini, reheating). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (2026–27). DPH will schedule a pre-opening inspection when construction is 80% complete; the inspector will verify that the kitchen layout, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and ventilation match the approved plans. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes, and service to the public cannot begin before issuance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the CUA is final and the building permit is issued, file the ABC Type 42 license transfer application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control and post the required 30-day public notice at 995 Valencia St. What to say: The license broker will prepare the ABC transfer application (person-to-person and premises-to-premises) with the escrow documents, lease, seller's permit, entity registration, and the approved CUA motion. ABC will send the application to SFPD (ABC Liaison Unit) and SF Planning for referral review; Planning will issue a letter confirming the CUA authorizes a Bar with Type 42 license under Mission SUD § 249.60(b)(2)(C). Post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days and mail copies to all residents and businesses within 500 ft. If no protests are filed, ABC will approve the transfer in 60 to 90 days. If a protest is filed alleging undue concentration or public convenience issues, budget an additional 60 to 120 days for a public hearing and a PCN finding from the Board of Supervisors.
outcomes.note: Records confirm Type 42 exists and Bar requires CU with transferred license in SUD, but do not state the posting, mailing, referral, document or timeline details.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, California seller's permit, EIN, RBS training for all alcohol servers, food handler cards, and ASCAP/BMI music licenses before opening. What to say: File the SF Business Registration online with the Treasurer & Tax Collector ($55 to $700 depending on projected gross receipts, plus $4 state fee) immediately after forming the legal entity. Obtain the EIN from the IRS (free, same-day online), then register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA (free, needed for the ABC application). Enroll all employees who will serve alcohol in the ABC RBS training ($3 registration plus $10 to $25 course fee per person) within 60 days of hire. Enroll all food-handling employees in the California Food Handler Card course ($7 to $15, valid 3 years). Designate at least one certified food safety manager (ServSafe exam, $100 to $250). Sign up for ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses (annual fees roughly $300 to $2,500 each, formula-based on occupancy and music use) to cover recorded and live music legally.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 185 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $7,941 to $23,750. Notes: The timeline and cost ranges cover the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000), Place of Entertainment permit (45 to 120 days, $2,708 to $3,800), Health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000), and Building permit with change of use (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000). The day range is the time to approval, not to a denial or withdrawal. The critical path is the CUA hearing (6 to 10 months from filing to final, including pre-application meeting, environmental review, neighborhood notification, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period) followed by the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60 to 150 days after the CUA is final, including escrow, posting, referrals, and undue-concentration review if protested). The POE permit hearing is scheduled in parallel with the CUA and decided within the same cycle. The building permit and health permit are filed after the CUA is approved and run concurrently during construction (3 to 6 months for plan review, build-out, and inspections). Total elapsed time from CUA filing to opening: roughly 12 to 18 months if the CUA and ABC transfer are approved without appeals or protests. Costs include the CUA fee ($3,100 base, higher if construction valuation exceeds thresholds or First Year Free fee waiver does not apply), POE application fee ($2,708 in 2026–27), building permit fees (percentage of construction cost, estimated $800 to $15,000 for a bar tenant improvement), DPH plan check ($828 to $2,207 depending on scope), Health Permit to Operate application ($470), and the ABC Type 42 license purchase price (not a government fee, estimated $20,000 to $60,000 based on market comparables for Type 42 transfers in San Francisco, excluded from the cost range here). Additional costs not in the range: architect and engineer fees for stamped plans, license broker commission (typically 10% to 15% of the license price), construction costs, and pre-opening legal and consultant fees. The cost range shown is government fees only.
